newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway oil reserves up 400 mln bbls in '96 - Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Norway oil reserves up 400 mln bbls in '96 - Statoil.

text.p: Exploration drilling from fixed and floating units off Norway in 1996 added about 400 million barrels of oil and 50 billion cubic metres of gas to Norwegian hydrocarbon reserves, state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.

Preliminary Statoil figures put the company's share of this volume amounted to just over 60 million barrels of crude and a little less than 10 billion cubic metres of gas, the Status Weekly newsletter said.
Most of the finds were close to producing fields in the North Sea.
"Exploration has once again made a positive contribution to the group's results," said Tor Gunnar Gloppen, Statoil licence manager.

The company will produce development and operation plans in 1996/97 for at least two of the new discoveries -- Statoil's largest find of the year in block 33/9 near Statfjord North and a small strike near Yme.
The group participated in 24 exploration or appraisal wells, including sidetracks, from mobile rigs in 1996 and was operator for 10. Three wells also were spudded from platforms on Yme and Gullfaks.
Five exploration wells drilled in 1995 were completed this year, Statoil said.
"Our discoveries are positive because several of them can be developed quickly and cheaply with the aid of existing installations making them very commercial," said Gloppen.
